summary: # CLO Skills Workshop - Making Elastic Drawstrings ## Introduction Hello everyone! In this workshop, I will show you how to make a spring-loaded plate for elastic drawstrings. ## Creating the Spring-Loaded Plate First, I have already converted the eye part of the face into a hole. Next, click on the 3D window and find the plate. Use the lift tool to create a spring-loaded plate. ### Drawing the Inner Lines Draw two inner lines at the front of the eye. The length of the inner line is the same as the width of the spring-loaded plate, which is 1.5. After drawing, you can see its position in the 3D window. Since the plate is in a moving state, the inner line is symmetrical. ### Attaching the Spring-Loaded Plate Next, sew the spring-loaded plate to the inner plate. Now, choose the spring-loaded plate in the 2D window. Use the quick arrangement tool next to the positioning ball in the 3D window to arrange the plate near the eye. ## Simulation and Adjustment To increase the simulation speed, you can use your sending Julia to check its position. Then, adjust the center position to the three-das, and press the Allen button to change the position. After the simulation time, let's explore creating the spring-loaded plate. ### Editing the Selection You can use the Edit Selection Tool to change the selection line and simulate it again. The other side requires the same operation. After the adjustment is complete, we will adjust the shape again. ### Shaping the Board Now, the board is a C-shape. Next, use the fixed needle tool. Add two fixed needles to the drawstring board. Use the Selection Tool to adjust its position and modify the board to the shape of a pass-through adjustment buckle. ## Further Adjustments You can also further reduce the strength of the drawstring board. Next, we will adjust the shape of the drawstring board. The fixed needle can be added in both the 3D and 2D windows. Continue to adjust its shape. ### Connecting the Components After the adjustment is almost done, we enter the Connect layer in the drawstring window. Add the adjusted buckle that has been added in advance. Select "Add to workspace" with six keys, select "Open," and use the glue tool to stick it directly on the drawboard. ### Finalizing the Position Adjust the size, and then use the positioning tool to adjust its position. In addition, in the 3D window, you can directly adjust the size of the component. Select this component in the object window, and in the attribute editor, you can accurately modify its size. ## Completing the Simulation Now, let's continue to adjust the position of the component. Insert the drawboard into the adjustment button. After the adjustment is complete, we can start the simulation. Since the component has already been pasted onto the drawboard, it is more visible. ### Detail Adjustments This is done according to the simulation of the drawboard. Now, let's adjust its details. After the adjustment is complete, we will add a rendering thickness to the drawboard. Now the horizontal drawstring is finished. ## Copying and Freezing the Boards Now directly press Ctrl + D to align the finished board and copy it. Similarly, the two boards of the hat will be frozen, and the previously made drawstring will be frozen. Let's simulate the parallel drawstring. ### Final Adjustments After the adjustment is complete, we can adjust the position of the component. Once again, after the adjustment is complete, we will freeze the drawstring board. Now, the parallel drawstring on both sides is completed. ## Adding the Eye Finally, let's add the eye of the eye. Use the twist tool to add the eye. We need to pay attention to this step: we need to turn off the twist of the tool. Then, use the positioning tool to adjust the position of the eye. ### Symmetrical Adjustment After the adjustment is complete, we will copy the twist to the board of the symmetrical adjustment. Similarly, we need to adjust its position on the other side. ## Conclusion Finally, we will activate all the boards. Our spring-loaded drawstring is now complete. Let's have a look at the final results. See you in the next video, and good luck!
